name: NEOS
full_name: Neutrino Experiment for Oscillation at Short Baseline
summary: NEOS used a compact liquid-scintillator detector near Hanbit to examine the reactor-antineutrino spectrum in two measurement campaigns. Its short-baseline spectrum tests eV-scale sterile mixing, while the NEOS-II full-fuel-cycle data also probe uranium/plutonium spectral evolution.
detection_principle: Gadolinium-loaded scintillator detects inverse beta decay with prompt and delayed light. Pulse-shape information and reactor-off data constrain cosmogenic and reactor-site backgrounds; the spectral ratio is fitted for disappearance distortions.

sites.name: South Korea; Hanbit nuclear power plant
sites.location: South Korea; Hanbit nuclear power plant

status.label: Completed measurement campaigns
status.evidence: NEOS-I ran in 2015–2016 and NEOS-II collected a complete fuel cycle from September 2018 to October 2020. This status refers to those documented campaigns; analysis continued afterwards.

timeline.event: NEOS-II recorded a full reactor fuel cycle
NEOS-II response and preliminary analysis reported at Neutrino 2022

collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

phases.name: NEOS-I
phases.description: August 2015–May 2016; first published spectral sterile-neutrino search.

phases.name: NEOS-II
phases.description: September 2018–October 2020; 388 reactor-on and 112 reactor-off live days in the 2022 detector-response report.

results.summary: The initial spectral comparison found no conclusive sterile-neutrino signal and constrained electron-antineutrino disappearance in the eV-scale region.
